root_idea.summary: A root oriented toward firmness, strength, power, and resistance, with related extensions involving overcoming, elevation, honor, and difficulty of access.
root_idea.development: The semantic field develops from being strong or hard to overcoming another, conferring strength or honor, being invulnerable or difficult to attain, and, in physical descriptions, hardness, compactness, or restricted flow.

senses.definition: To overcome or prevail over someone in an argument or dispute.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic expression عَزَّنِي فِي الْخِطَابِ, the verb describes gaining the upper hand in verbal contention.

senses.definition: To strengthen, reinforce, or render mighty.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic construction فَعَزَّزْنَا بِثَالِثٍ describes reinforcing a group by means of a third person.

senses.definition: To confer might, honor, or elevated standing upon someone.
senses.usage_conditions: In تُعِزُّ مَنْ تَشَاءُ, the verb is contrasted with يُذِلُّ and denotes granting a person might or honor.
A comparative form used in comparisons of power, strength, or honor.
Used broadly as an adjective and as a divine name; when applied to God, it denotes the One who overcomes all and is not overcome.
In عَزِيزٌ عَلَيْهِ مَا عَنِتُّمْ, the construction means that what burdens or troubles others is grievous to him; the same adjective can describe severe circumstances.

senses.definition: Inimitable, secure, and not liable to be nullified or corrupted.
senses.usage_conditions: In كِتَابٌ عَزِيزٌ, the adjective characterizes the Book as mighty, inaccessible to imitation, and protected from invalidation or corruption.

senses.definition: A ruler or royal official; in the Joseph narrative, the title of the ruler of Egypt.
senses.usage_conditions: A conventional title in the expression الْعَزِيز, rather than an ordinary descriptive adjective.

senses.definition: Firm, unyielding, or proud in dealing with opponents.
senses.usage_conditions: In أَعِزَّةٍ عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ, the quality is paired with gentleness toward believers and describes resolute, non-submissive conduct toward unbelievers.

senses.definition: Might, power, honor, or protective strength.
senses.usage_conditions: In لِيَكُونُوا لَهُمْ عِزًّا, the noun denotes a sought source of power or protection, including protection from punishment.

senses.definition: Might, honor, dignity, or inviolable standing.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of the lasting might and honor attributed to God, His Messenger, and believers, and as the quality sought or possessed by a community.

senses.definition: Self-exalting pride, haughtiness, or obstinate self-importance.
senses.usage_conditions: A blameworthy use, especially in أَخَذَتْهُ الْعِزَّةُ بِالْإِثْمِ and فِي عِزَّةٍ وَشِقَاقٍ; it denotes asserted superiority rather than genuine, enduring honor.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become mighty, powerful, elevated in rank, noble, or honorable, especially after weakness or low status.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive Form I use describing acquired or restored strength, potency, elevation, or social standing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To surpass someone in nobility or generosity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A construction describing superiority in personal excellence rather than physical strength.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To magnify or exalt oneself; to become disdainful, scornful, or blamefully indignant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative and blameworthy self-directed use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become weak.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An attested contrary sense of the otherwise strength-oriented Form I verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To distress, afflict, or weigh heavily upon someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Usually followed by عَلَى and an event or circumstance; it can express grief, difficulty, or indignation at what has occurred.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become difficult, hard, impossible, insuperable, or unattainable.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of a thing or undertaking that cannot readily be overcome or achieved.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become rare, scarce, or hard to find; hence to be highly valued or dear.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The rarity sense concerns limited availability, while the derived valuation concerns what is prized because it is uncommon.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To aid or help someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive use distinct from overcoming an opponent.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For water to flow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A physical use describing the movement of water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a wound or pustule to discharge its contents.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of the wound or pustule as it releases what is within it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a she-camel, ewe, or goat: to have constricted teats and yield little milk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A livestock expression concerning restricted milk flow; it is also used figuratively of a wealthy but niggardly person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a cow: to have difficult or abnormal gestation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form IV livestock use with disagreement in the reports over whether the gestation is merely difficult or specifically bad.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a goat or ewe: to show pregnancy and become enlarged in the udder.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A livestock use describing visible pregnancy or the associated enlargement of the udder.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For rain to make earth compact, coherent, and hard.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object is land or ground made firm so that feet do not sink into it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To treat people with hardness, severity, or rigor rather than indulgence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive or passive construction describing strict treatment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To love someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported Form IV sense qualified in the source as weak or less firmly established.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To enter or travel through hard ground of the type called عَزَاز.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb describes being or journeying in such terrain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To strengthen or fortify oneself; to draw strength or energy from something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The form may describe relying on divine strength or exerting one's own energy.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To magnify or harden oneself and behave proudly or harshly toward others; to glory or pride oneself in someone or something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reflexive or figurative use involving self-assertion, pride, or reliance on a source of prestige.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To force oneself to endure the loss or absence of someone or something patiently.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional development in which exerting one's strength becomes consoling oneself and bearing a loss.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For the flesh of a she-camel to become hard or tough.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A physical use describing the texture of flesh.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To reckon oneself strong or mighty by means of another person or thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The preposition بِ identifies the person or resource regarded as a source of strength.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For disease to become violent or severe and overcome someone; by extension, for someone to be overcome by illness or die.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The passive form describes a person overcome by disease; the active construction presents the disease as prevailing over him.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For sand or another loose material to hold together or cohere instead of pouring down.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A physical use describing compacted or self-supporting sand and similar material.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Resistance, invincibility, or the quality of not being overcome; hence the difficulty or impossibility of overcoming or attaining something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal branch emphasizing resistance and inaccessibility rather than honor as a social quality.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Vehement or copious rain, and an overpowering torrent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to rain or a torrent that is forceful and overwhelming.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Compelled or brought about without any means of avoiding it, willingly or unwillingly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fixed idiom conveying unavoidable compulsion, originally associated with being overcome and despoiled.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The female young one of a gazelle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate nominal homonym distinguished by its short vowel pattern from عِزَّة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Difficult, impossible, or unattainable; resistant to being overcome.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A broader adjectival branch of عزيز concerning inaccessibility or insuperability.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Rare, scarce, extraordinary, or highly valued.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The sense extends from rarity to something dear or esteemed because it is uncommon or unequalled.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Rough, proud, disdainful, or scornful in manner.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A descriptive adjectival use of personal bearing, distinct from the Quranic paired conduct toward believers and unbelievers.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hard, firm, rugged ground, especially ground on which rain quickly runs off.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: مَعْزُوزَةٌ may also describe ground made compact and hard by heavy rain; the terrain is often at the borders or elevated parts of a tract.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A small watercourse of a valley, shorter than a مِذْنَب.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A geographical or topographical term for a short runoff channel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The small sweet tubers of cyperus esculentus, or the plant producing them.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A later technical or common name for the tuber and plant.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An eagle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare lexical use, with variant reports connecting the word to a bird that has gone far from its pursuer or to a dark-colored bird.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The extremity or anatomical region of a horse's hip or haunch, including the part between the tail-root and the posterior cleft.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The terms may also denote a sinew extending from the rectum to the hip; their dual forms preserve the distinction in reference.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The name of a pre-Islamic idol, associated with Quraysh and other Arab groups; also associated with a sacred acacia tree.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A proper name with variant accounts of its cult site and form; it is not the ordinary comparative adjective.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The One who grants might or honor to whomever He wills among His servants.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A divine name formed from the Form IV causative pattern.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cause or means of might, honor, or strengthening.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An analogically derived noun for that which produces عزّ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who reckons himself strong or empowered through another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The participial form corresponds to اِعْتَزَّ بِهِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a mare: having thick and strong flesh.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A physical adjectival use applied to an animal's build.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Pointer-only cross-reference to the livestock sense.

cautions: عَزِيزٌ has several Quran-attested uses: general might, a title in the Joseph narrative, grievousness in عَزِيزٌ عَلَيْهِ, the characterization of the Book, and resolute conduct toward opponents; these should not be collapsed into a single English gloss.
Several Lane citations use historical bracketed references; no such notation has been converted into a modern verse location without an independently supplied QAC location.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: The reported Form IV sense أَعَزَّ meaning “to love” is retained as a broader Classical meaning but is qualified in the evidence as weak.

Lane reports variant interpretations for the Form IV livestock uses concerning gestation and pregnancy; they are represented as distinct qualified lexical branches rather than forced into one interpretation.
